_readme: Per-locale policy for the em dash in editorial copy, read by scripts/check-editorial-footprint.js (enforcement, forward-only) and scripts/audit-em-dash.js (measurement). Adopted by the user on 2026-09-02 from the table in docs/em-dash-policy.md §4 and meant to be revised as more pages are crawled: a locale changes policy only with a dated edit here, a native reader's confirmation or corpus evidence, and an entry in the doc's change log. `policy` is one of the four keys in `policies`. `replacement` is what the gate tells an author to write instead and is null where no rule exists. `nextReview` is the date the row is re-read against the audit. Every canonical locale must have an entry; a locale without one is treated as `review` and reported as missing.

policies.ban: a new em dash a branch introduces in editorial copy fails the check, in every mode (forward-only; existing ones are reported, never billed). The gate names the locale's native replacement.
policies.native: the em dash is native punctuation in this language; it is never a finding.
policies.double-dash: the native dash is the paired form ——; a new lone — fails the check, a new —— does not.
policies.review: a new em dash is reported as a warning only, pending a native reader or corpus evidence.

en.nativeMark: none in new copy: the em dash is the pattern being removed
en.replacement: a colon when what follows explains; a full stop for a separate thought; a comma pair for an aside; parentheses for a parenthetical; an en dash ( – ) for a range
en.basis: house style; user decision 2026-09-02; 9,682 existing em dashes on 889 of 911 pages reported and never billed

ru.nativeMark: — (тире), spaced; replaces an omitted copula, opens dialogue, marks ranges
ru.basis: Правила русской орфографии и пунктуации; corpus median 28.9 per 1,000 words, the highest on the site

es.nativeMark: — (raya) for dialogue and incisos; expository web prose leans on commas and parentheses
es.basis: RAE, Ortografía de la lengua española; corpus median 10.9 per 1,000 words, the lowest Latin-script rate here

pt.basis: standard Brazilian and European usage; corpus median 16.0

fr.basis: Lexique des règles typographiques (Imprimerie nationale); corpus median 16.0

pl.nativeMark: — or  –  (myślnik); dashes are frequent in Polish prose
pl.basis: Wielki słownik ortograficzny PWN; corpus median 23.1

ro.nativeMark: — or  –  (linia de pauză) for asides and dialogue
